title: Tidemark Account Credit on Excess Flood Renewals
content:
An **Excess Flood Policies (Surplus Lines)** renewal earns an account credit where the primary flood policy beneath the layer is also written by Tidemark.

**Rule.** The renewal account adjustment is a credit of 7 percent where the HomeFlood policy of the home exists, a credit of 4 percent where it does not but the NFIP policy of the home exists, and nothing otherwise.

The NFIP policy of the home is the Tidemark NFIP Dwelling Form policy (NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own)) in force whose policy number is the underlying policy number on the excess policy record, and the HomeFlood policy of the home is the active Tidemark HomeFlood policy (HomeFlood Private Residential Flood Policies) whose policy number is that underlying policy number; of these two policies only their status, the NFIP policy's primary-residence designation, their claim payments and voided payments and the NFIP policy's applied Elevation Certificates are read. Where two entries on a file share the date they are read by, or two policy records answer the same description, the one entered first is read.

| Primary policy found under the excess policy's underlying policy number | Adjustment entered (percent) |
|---|---|
| an active Tidemark HomeFlood policy (HomeFlood Private Residential Flood Policies) | -7, a credit of 7 percent |
| no such HomeFlood policy, but a Tidemark NFIP Dwelling Form policy in force (NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own)) | -4, a credit of 4 percent |
| neither | no account adjustment |

Every percentage selected for a renewal term is added into one net adjustment percentage, which acts once on the zone-factored layer charge after the elevation multiplier — that charge is multiplied by one plus the net adjustment percentage — and never on the loss-of-use charge.

**Basis questions answered.** Does a HomeFlood policy on the home that is not active count? No — the HomeFlood policy of the home is the active one. Does an NFIP Dwelling Form policy on the same address under a different policy number count? No — both policies are identified by the underlying policy number on the excess policy record. Where both an active HomeFlood policy and an NFIP policy in force answer, the 7 percent credit applies.
